Oxidation and reduction in terms of oxidation numbers Activity:
a. Find the oxidation number of Fe and Cr in both reactants and products. b. Identify whether there is increase or decrease in oxidation number in these atoms during

the chemical reaction. If an atom gains electrons, the oxidation number decreases. Similarly, if an atom loses electrons, the oxidation number increases. Oxidation is the increase in oxidation number and reduction is the decrease in oxidation number.

Oxidation number of iron decreases from +3 to +2. It means iron (III) chloride is reduced to iron (II) chloride so FeCl3 is an oxidising agent. Likewise, the oxidation number of tin increases from +2 to +4. It means tin (II) chloride is oxidised to tin (IV) chloride so it is called a reducing agent.
